newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to meet Japanese Venalum partners Tues.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to meet Japanese Venalum partners Tues.

text.p: Venezuelan officials will meet representatives of the Japanese consortium that owns 20 percent of aluminum smelter Venalum in New York on September 24, the Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) said on Friday.
The FIV said the three days of meetings that start next Tuesday will reach a definite agreement on the Japanese consortium's power of veto over the 430,000 tonnes per year capacity smelter.
The New York talks follow negotiations in Tokyo last month that broke down without reaching agreement.

The Japanese consortium is seeking financial compensation for the removal of its veto power and wants the Venezuelan government to re-start shipments of a 90,000 tonnes per year contract, which was suspended in February.
The Venezuelan government plans to sell a controlling stake in Venalum, along with smelter Alcasa, carbon anode producer Carbonorca and bauxite and alumina producer Bauxilum in December.

The FIV announced on Wednesday that 13 companies had qualified to bid for the four-company aluminum sector including Aluminum Co of America (Alcoa), Gencor Ltd, Glencore Ltd, Reynolds Metals Co, Norsk Hydro ASA, and RTZ Corp- CRA Ltd.
The FIV has not said how much the aluminum sector sale could fetch, but analysts have valued the four companies at about $2 billion.

The Japanese consortium, which owns the 20 percent stake in Venalum includes Showa Denko KK, Kobe Steel Ltd, Sumitomo Chemical Co Ltd, Mitsubishi Materials Corp, Mitsubishi Aluminum Co Ltd and Marubeni Corp.
